heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Indonesia
heroData.subtitle: Hire in Jakarta, Bali & Surabaya
heroData.description: Compliant employment in Indonesia. We manage the complex BPJS contributions, mandatory THR allowances, and OmniBus Law compliance to get you operational in days.

steps.title: Contract Classification
steps.description: Choose between Fixed-Term (PKWT) or Indefinite (PKWTT) contracts. Fixed-term contracts are now capped at 5 years total under the OmniBus Law. Contracts MUST be in Bahasa Indonesia or bilingual.

steps.title: BPJS Health & Labor Registration
steps.description: Register employees for BPJS Kesehatan (Health) and BPJS Ketenagakerjaan (including Pension, Old Age, Death, and Work Accident). Registration must happen before the first payday.

steps.title: Tax Identification (NPWP)
steps.description: Verify the employee's Tax ID. If the employee doesn't have one, the PPh 21 tax rate is 20% higher. The EOR can assist in obtaining this digitally.

steps.title: Mandatory Tapera Setup
steps.description: New for 2025: Enroll employees in the Public Housing Savings (Tapera) program. Private sector participation is mandatory by 2027, but many EORs are opting in now.

items.title: Maintaining 'Face'
items.text: Criticism should always be private and subtle. Public confrontation is avoided to maintain 'harmony' (Rukun).

items.title: Hierarchical Respect
items.text: Seniority is highly valued. Use 'Bapak' (Mr.) or 'Ibu' (Ms/Mrs) before the employee's name in official communication.

items.title: Indirect Communication
items.text: A 'Yes' might sometimes mean 'I understand' rather than 'I agree'. Build deep relationships to understand true intent.

items.title: 3+3 Maternity Leave
items.text: New regulation provides 3 months full pay followed by an optional 3 months at 75% pay for mothers with health issues or childcare needs.

items.title: THR Timing
items.text: The Religious Holiday Allowance must be paid NO LATER than 7 days before the holiday. Late payment results in a 5% penalty.

items.title: Paternity Leave
items.text: Standard paternity leave is 2 days, but many progressive companies are offering 1-2 weeks to stay competitive.

items.title: Contractor Misclassification
items.text: Hiring Indonesian residents as 'independent contractors' for full-time roles can lead to reclassification as permanent employees, triggering backdated BPJS and severance liabilities.

items.title: Economic Dependence Test
items.text: If a worker relies solely on one foreign company for income and uses company equipment, Indonesian labor courts are highly likely to rule them as an employee.

items.title: Compliant Transition
items.text: Moving contractors to an EOR model is the standard 'safe harbor' for international companies scaling in Indonesia.

faqs.question: Can I hire foreign workers through an EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the EOR must process a RPTKA (utilization plan) and KITAS (stay permit). It typically takes 4-8 weeks.

faqs.question: What is the probation period limit?
faqs.answer: Probation is only allowed for Indefinite (PKWTT) contracts and is capped at 3 months. Fixed-term (PKWT) contracts cannot have probation.

faqs.question: Can I terminate an employee easily?
faqs.answer: No. Indonesia has strict labor laws. Termination requires proven grounds, a 14-day notice, and often substantial severance pay.

faqs.question: What is 'Cuti Bersama'?
faqs.answer: It refers to 'Joint Leave' holidays declared by the government, which are usually deducted from the employee's 12-day annual leave entitlement.

faqs.question: Are there mandatory medical check-ups?
faqs.answer: Yes, Indonesian Labor Law technically requires employees to undergo a medical check-up once a year, paid for by the employer.

faqs.question: Can I use foreign employment contracts?
faqs.answer: No. Under Law No. 24 of 2009, all contracts must be in Bahasa Indonesia (or bilingual). Using only a foreign law contract is legally void.

faqs.question: What is the notice period for PKWT?
faqs.answer: Fixed-term (PKWT) contracts don't technically have a notice period; if either party terminates early, they must pay the remaining salary of the contract term.

steps.title: Category Identification
steps.description: Identify if the employee falls under Category A, B, or C based on their PTKP status (dependents).

steps.title: Monthly TER Application
steps.description: Apply the Monthly Effective Rate (0% to 34%) to the gross income for Jan-Nov.

steps.title: Annual Recalculation
steps.description: In December, calculate tax using the traditional progressive Article 17 rates and subtract what was paid in Jan-Nov.

items.title: Tax Filing (SPT Masa)
items.text: Must be filed by the 20th of the following month. Late filing results in a IDR 100,000 penalty per month.

items.title: BPJS Payment Deadline
items.text: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan is due by the 15th, and BPJS Kesehatan by the 10th of the following month.

items.title: Annual Form 1721-A1
items.text: Provide employees with their annual tax form (1721-A1) no later than January or February following the tax year.

items.title: Bilingual Payslips
items.description: While not strictly mandatory for all, providing payslips in both English and Bahasa Indonesia is best practice for foreign-owned entities.

items.title: BPJS Certificate (Sertifikat BPJS)
items.description: Ensure your entity has a valid certificate for both Health and Labor to avoid issues during annual company audits.

items.title: Monthly Tax Payment Slips (SSP)
items.description: Digital copies of Surat Setoran Pajak (SSP) must be archived for 10 years as proof of PPh 21 remittance.

items.title: The 'THR' Expectation
items.description: Employees view THR as a performance-unrelated right. Reducing THR for performance reasons is highly contentious.

items.title: Bank Mandate
items.description: State-owned banks (Mandiri, BNI) are often preferred for government-linked payments, though BCA is the retail favorite.

items.title: Overtime Approval
items.description: Always have signed Overtime Orders. Verbal agreements for overtime are difficult to defend in labor court.

faqs.question: What is the PTKP for 2025?
faqs.answer: The standard non-taxable income (TK/0) is IDR 54,000,000 per year, which is IDR 4,500,000 per month.

faqs.question: Are fixed allowances taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes. All fixed and variable allowances (transport, meal, housing) are included in the gross income for PPh 21 calculation.

faqs.question: Is payslip mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, under Government Regulation No. 36 of 2021, employers must provide a proof of salary payment containing details of earnings and deductions.

faqs.question: Can I pay in USD?
faqs.answer: No. Law No. 7 of 2011 mandates the use of IDR for all transactions within Indonesia, including salary payments.

faqs.question: What happens if a payday falls on a weekend?
faqs.answer: Standard practice is to pay on the last working day before the weekend or holiday to ensure compliance with 'timely payment' rules.

faqs.question: How do I handle expense reimbursements?
faqs.answer: Reimbursements are usually processed alongside payroll. If they are business-related and supported by valid invoices, they are not subject to PPh 21 tax.

faqs.question: Is the 13th-month pay mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the employee has worked for at least 1 month. It is called THR (Tunjangan Hari Raya) and is paid before the major religious holiday.

steps.title: Calculate Gross Pay
steps.description: Sum of Base Salary + Fixed Allowances (Transport, Meal, Work-from-home).

steps.title: Determine TER Category
steps.description: Assign Category A (Unmarried/No kids), B (Married/1-2 kids), or C (Married/3 kids) based on PTKP status.

steps.title: Apply Monthly TER Rate
steps.description: Select the percentage (0% to 34%) from the government table corresponding to the Gross Pay and Category.

steps.title: BPJS Deductions
steps.description: Subtract 1.0% for Health (Kesehatan) and 1.0% for Pension (JP), and 2.0% for Old Age (JHT) from the employee's gross.

steps.title: Calculate Net Pay
steps.description: Gross Pay - TER Tax - BPJS Employee Contributions = Take-home pay.

items.title: TK/0 (Single)
items.description: IDR 54,000,000 annually (~IDR 4.5M monthly).

items.title: K/0 (Married)
items.description: IDR 58,500,000 annually.

items.title: K/3 (Married + 3 Children)
items.description: IDR 72,000,000 annually (Maximum threshold).

items.title: TER Category Accuracy
items.text: Selecting the wrong category (A, B, or C) can lead to tax variances of up to 5% of gross salary.

items.title: BPJS Caps
items.text: The calculator automatically applies the IDR 12M cap for health and IDR 10.5M cap for pension calculations.

items.title: December Reconciliation
items.text: A manual true-up is always required in December to align the monthly TER totals with the annual Art 17 calculation.

items.title: Rounding Rules
items.description: Indonesian tax calculations typically round down to the nearest thousand for taxable income (PKP).

items.title: Net vs Gross Contracts
items.description: Most calculators assume a 'Gross' contract. 'Net' contracts require 'Gross-up' logic which is significantly more complex.

items.title: Currency Fluctuations
items.description: If the contract is in USD but paid in IDR, use the KMK (Ministry of Finance) exchange rate for tax reporting.

faqs.question: Why is the tax lower in Jan-Nov?
faqs.answer: The TER method simplifies monthly withholding. In December, a 'true-up' calculation occurs which may lead to higher or lower tax in the final month.

faqs.question: Is insurance deductible from tax?
faqs.answer: BPJS Old Age (JHT) and Pension (JP) contributions are deductible from the gross income before applying the Article 17 annual calculation.

faqs.question: Does the calculator handle THR?
faqs.answer: Yes. THR is added to the regular monthly income and taxable under the same TER table for the month it is paid.

heroData.title: Entity Setup Indonesia
heroData.subtitle: PT PMA & RO Solutions
heroData.description: Navigate the updated capital requirements of 2025 to establish your foreign-owned company in the world's 4th most populous nation.

items.title: PT PMA
items.text: Foreign Investment Company. Can generate revenue, sponsor visas, and own property (HGB). Requires min investment IDR 10 billion.

items.title: KPPA (Representative Office)
items.text: Liaison office. Cannot generate revenue or issue invoices. Used for market research and brand presence.

items.title: EOR as Alternative
items.text: If you need to hire immediately without the $650k capital commitment, use an EOR until you are ready to incorporate.

steps.title: Name Approval
steps.description: Check and reserve company name with Ministry of Law and Human Rights (SABH).

steps.title: Deed of Establishment
steps.description: Draft and sign the Deed (Akta) before an Indonesian Notary. Details of shareholders and directors are formalized here.

steps.title: NIB Issuance (OSS RBA)
steps.description: Register via the Online Single Submission (OSS) system to obtain the Business ID Number (NIB), which serves as your import license and operational permit.

steps.title: Bank Account Setup
steps.description: Open a local IDR and USD account. Large banks like Mandiri or BCA are recommended for digital features.

items.title: Annual LKPM Reporting
items.description: Mandatory quarterly Investment Activity Reports (LKPM) via the OSS system. Failure to file can lead to NIB suspension.

items.title: Ratification of Articles
items.description: Any change in shareholders or directors must be ratified by the Ministry of Law (SK Kemenkumham).

items.title: Local Domicile Letter
items.description: In certain regions outside Jakarta, a 'Domisili' letter from the local sub-district (Kelurahan) is still required.

items.title: The 'Pajak' Landscape
items.description: Building a good relationship with your local 'Account Representative' (AR) at the tax office is as important as the filings themselves.

items.title: Networking (KADIN)
items.description: Joining the Indonesian Chamber of Commerce (KADIN) or specific business associations (like AmCham) is highly recommended for PT PMAs.

items.title: The Role of OJK
items.description: If your entity involves Fintech or multi-finance, you will need secondary licenses from the Financial Services Authority (OJK) which are notoriously slow.

faqs.question: Can a PT PMA be 100% foreign owned?
faqs.answer: Yes, for most sectors under the 2021 Positive Investment List, 100% ownership is allowed. Some sectors (e.g., small-scale tourism) remain closed or restricted.

faqs.question: Do I need a local director?
faqs.answer: No. Directors and Commissioners can be foreigners, but at least one person must have an Indonesian Tax ID (NPWP) for administrative filings.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most regions (especially Jakarta) require a commercial office address. Virtual offices are permitted for certain business classifications (KBLI).

faqs.question: What is a 'NIB'?
faqs.answer: Business Identification Number (Nomor Induk Berusaha). It serves as your TDP (Company Reg), API (Import License), and NPI (Customs Access).

faqs.question: Can I change my business activity later?
faqs.answer: Yes, by amending your Articles of Association and updating your OSS (Online Single Submission) profile, which may require additional capital injection.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capital for PT PMA?
faqs.answer: IDR 10 Billion (approx. USD 650k). At least 25% (IDR 2.5 Billion) must be paid-up capital and proven to the authorities.

heroData.title: Staffing & Recruitment
heroData.subtitle: Jakarta's Tech Talent
heroData.description: Source top-tier talent in Southeast Asia's largest economy. From engineering hubs in Jakarta to creative talent in Bali, we bridge the gap between global standards and local expertise.

steps.title: Sourcing Strategy
steps.description: Leverage LinkedIn, Glints, and Tech in Asia for digital roles. For traditional industries, local networks (KADIN) are essential.

steps.title: Technical Assessment
steps.description: Mandatory for tech roles. Indonesian candidates often prefer take-home assignments over live coding.

steps.title: Cultural Fit & BPJS Check
steps.description: Verify existing BPJS status and expectations regarding THR (13th-month pay) which is strictly mandatory.

steps.title: The 'Offer' Ceremony
steps.description: Personal touches matter. Often, a verbal 'intent' call precedes the formal offer letter to ensure alignment with family expectations.

items.title: Healthcare Plus
items.description: Private insurance (Manulife/Allianz) on top of BPJS is the #1 requested benefit for mid-senior talent.

items.title: Training Budget
items.description: Indonesian talent values upskilling. Certifications (AWS, PMP) are highly prized.

items.title: Religious Leave
items.description: Respecting 'Mudik' (homecoming) during Eid al-Fitr is critical for long-term employee loyalty.

items.title: SCBD & Mega Kuningan
items.text: The 'Silicon Valley' of Jakarta. Home to GoTo, Traveloka, and major fintechs. Salaries are 20-30% higher here.

items.title: Jogja & Bandung
items.text: Emerging tech hubs for remote engineering teams. Lower overheads and high-quality alumni from ITB and UGM.

items.title: Bali Remote Scene
items.text: A global hotspot for creative and design talent. Digital Nomad Visas have made it easier to hire international talent locally.

items.title: Family Influence
items.description: Many Indonesian professionals consult their families before accepting an offer. Be prepared for longer decision times if family approval is needed.

items.title: LinkedIn is Critical
items.description: While many platforms exist, LinkedIn is the primary tool for white-collar talent acquisition in Jakarta and Surabaya.

items.title: Cultural Harmony
items.description: Questions about religious holidays and family commitments are common during interviews and should be handled with cultural sensitivity.

faqs.question: What is the typical notice period?
faqs.answer: 1 month for junior/mid-level, 2-3 months for senior management roles is standard practice.

faqs.question: Is LinkedIn popular in Indonesia?
faqs.answer: Extremely. It is the primary professional network, especially for white-collar talent in major cities.

faqs.question: Are background checks common?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially verifying employment history and educational credentials (Ijazah).

faqs.question: How long does it take to find a developer?
faqs.answer: For mid-level developers in Jakarta, expect 4-8 weeks. Senior talent or niche roles (AI/DevOps) can take 3+ months.

faqs.question: Do I need to pay for recruitment fees upfront?
faqs.answer: Most Indonesian agencies work on a success-fee basis (15-25% of annual salary), though some require a small retainer for executive search.

faqs.question: Are reference checks legally restricted?
faqs.answer: No, but it is best practice to obtain candidate consent under the new PDP (Data Privacy) Law before contacting previous employers.

heroData.title: HRIS & People Software
heroData.subtitle: Localized Automation
heroData.description: Streamline operations with platforms that natively handle Indonesian labor laws, from the OmniBus Law calculations to PPh 21 TER filing.

items.title: DJP Direct Integration
items.description: Direct upload of CSV files to e-Spt for Article 21 income tax filing.

items.title: Attendance with Geofencing
items.description: Mobile check-ins with face recognition, essential for managing Jakarta's mobile workforce.

items.title: THR Accrual Engine
items.description: Automated pro-rata calculation for the mandatory 13th-month Religious Holiday Allowance.

steps.title: Master Data Import
steps.description: Import employee NPWP (Tax ID), NIK (ID Card), and existing BPJS numbers.

steps.title: Policy Configuration
steps.description: Set up 'Cuti Bersama' (Joint Leave) and specific shift patterns according to the MOM guidelines.

steps.title: TER Tax Mapping
steps.description: Assign employees to Category A, B, or C for the 2024 Effective Tax Rate methodology.

steps.title: UAT & Parallel Run
steps.description: Run the new HRIS alongside legacy manual sheets for 1 month to ensure calculation parity.

items.title: Mekari Talenta
items.text: The market leader in Indonesia. Deeply integrated with local banks and the tax office.

items.title: GreatDay HR
items.text: Strength in mobile-first attendance and geofencing for field-heavy workforces.

items.title: Global vs Local
items.text: While Workday is great for global HQ, it often lacks the granular BPJS/PPh 21 logic required for local Indonesian compliance.

items.title: Offline-First Mobile
items.description: Ensure the app works in areas with poor internet connectivity, a common issue for field workers outside Jakarta.

items.title: Customer Support (WA)
items.description: Look for providers that offer WhatsApp-based support, as it is the preferred communication channel for most Indonesian HR managers.

items.title: Data Residency
items.description: Verify if the provider complies with Indonesia's PDP Law regarding local data storage for sensitive employee information.

faqs.question: Can I use an offshore HRIS for Indonesia?
faqs.answer: You can, but you will likely need a 'shadow payroll' or local middleware to handle the PPh 21 and BPJS calculations which are unique to Indonesia.

faqs.question: Does HRIS handle Tapera?
faqs.answer: Leading Indonesian HRIS systems like Talenta have already updated their modules for the 2025 Tapera requirements.

faqs.question: Is cloud storage compliant?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the software complies with Indonesia's PDP (Personal Data Protection) Law. Most major local providers use regional AWS/Google Cloud servers.

heroData.title: Accounting & Bookkeeping
heroData.subtitle: PSAK & IFRS Standards
heroData.description: Ensure your Indonesian operations meet the complex PSAK standards with rigorous monthly reconciliation and annual audit preparation.

steps.title: Transaction Recording
steps.description: Categorize expenses according to KBLI business lines and ensure VAT (PPN) info is captured.

steps.title: Withholding Tax Check
steps.description: Verify PPh 23 (Services) and PPh 4(2) (Rent) withholdings are correctly deducted from vendor payments.

steps.title: Bank Reconciliation
steps.description: Match IDR and USD accounts. Address exchange rate gains/losses according to PSAK 10.

steps.title: Final Reporting
steps.description: Generate Balance Sheet, P&L, and Cash Flow. File monthly tax returns (SPT Masa).

items.title: Mandatory Audit
items.text: PT PMAs (Foreign Investment Companies) are generally required to undergo an annual audit by a Public Accountant (KAP).

items.title: PSAK Framework
items.text: Indonesian Financial Accounting Standards (PSAK) are now largely converged with IFRS, making group consolidation easier.

items.title: Cloud Accounting
items.text: Xero and QuickBooks are popular for startups, but Jurnal.id is often preferred for its built-in Indonesian tax reporting.

items.title: Trial Balance
items.description: Detailed breakdown of all ledger accounts including intercompany transactions.

items.title: Fixed Asset Register
items.description: Maintenance of depreciation schedules according to fiscal tax categories (Group 1-4).

items.title: Account Payables
items.description: Aging report with specific focus on vendor tax ID (NPWP) verification.

items.title: Physical Archive
items.description: The '10-year physical record' rule is strictly enforced during tax audits. Invest in high-quality filing cabinets or secure storage.

items.title: Stamp Duty (Meterai)
items.description: Ensure all legal contracts and financial receipts above IDR 5M are stamped with the IDR 10,000 Meterai for legal standing.

items.title: Bilingual Ledger
items.description: Maintaining a bilingual chart of accounts saves significant time during group audit consolidations.

faqs.question: When does the fiscal year end?
faqs.answer: The standard fiscal year in Indonesia is January 1 to December 31. Permission from the tax office is required to change it.

faqs.question: What are the Big 4 in Indonesia?
faqs.answer: Deloitte (Imansyah), EY (Tanudiredja), KPMG (Siddharta), and PwC (Tanudiredja) all have large operations in Jakarta.

faqs.question: Do I need to keep physical records?
faqs.answer: Yes. While digital records are common, Indonesia still requires physical accounting books and supporting documents to be kept for 10 years.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late financial reporting?
faqs.answer: Administrative penalties apply at the Ministry of Law and Human Rights (AHU), and chronic late filing can lead to business license suspension.

faqs.question: Can I use IFRS instead of PSAK?
faqs.answer: While PSAK is largely aligned with IFRS, foreign companies must use PSAK for local statutory filings. IFRS is typically used for group reporting.

steps.title: Base Pay (UP)
steps.description: Calculated as 1 month salary for every year of service, capped at 9 months.

steps.title: Service Appreciation (UPMK)
steps.description: Starts after 3 years of service. Typically 2 months salary for the first 3-6 years.

steps.title: Compensation Rights (UPH)
steps.description: Payout for unused annual leave and relocation costs (if applicable).

steps.title: Reason-Based Multiplier
steps.description: Under OmniBus Law, multipliers (e.g., 0.5x, 0.75x, 1x) are applied based on the reason (Efficiency, Bankruptcy, or Breach).

items.title: Oct 2024/2025 Deadline
items.text: Full enforcement of the Personal Data Protection Law. Companies must appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO).

items.title: Cross-Border Transfer
items.text: Exporting Indonesian employee data requires ensuring the destination country has 'equivalent protection' or obtaining explicit consent.

items.title: Sanctions
items.text: Non-compliance can lead to fines up to 2% of annual turnover or criminal liability for directors.

items.title: Overtime Caps
items.description: Max 4 hours per day or 18 hours per week. Must be explicitly agreed upon (SPT/Overtime Order).

items.title: Rest Periods
items.description: Mandatory 30-minute break after 4 hours of work. Weekly rest of at least 1 day for 6-day weeks.

items.title: Workweek Options
items.description: 40 hours total: either 7 hours/day for 6 days or 8 hours/day for 5 days.

items.title: Joint Inspection (Sidak)
items.description: Manpower officials may conduct spot checks. Ensure copies of NIK, NPWP, and employment contracts (PKWT/PKWTT) are accessible on-site.

items.title: Bipartite Cooperation
items.description: Companies with >50 employees are encouraged to form a Bipartite Cooperation Forum (LKS Bipartit) to handle industrial relations.

items.title: Religious Holidays
items.description: Respect the 'Cuti Bersama' government decrees. While technically optional for the private sector, most companies align to maintain morale.

faqs.question: Are electronic signatures valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the ITE Law. Certified signatures (e.g., PrivyID, Vida) have higher evidentiary weight in Indonesian courts.

faqs.question: What is 'Wajib Lapor'?
faqs.answer: Mandatory Manpower Report (WLKP). Every entity must file this annually via the Kemnaker's online portal.

faqs.question: Is insurance for expats mandatory?
faqs.answer: Expats must be enrolled in BPJS Ketenagakerjaan if they work in Indonesia for >6 months, but BPJS Kesehatan is often complemented by private insurance.

items.title: Super Tax Deduction
items.text: Up to 200-300% deduction for R&D and vocational training activities in Indonesia.

items.title: IKN (New Capital) Holidays
items.text: Investment in Nusantara (IKN) can grant 100% CIT reduction for up to 30 years depending on the sector.

items.title: SEZ Benefits
items.text: Special Economic Zones like Galang Batang or Sanur offer VAT exemptions and specialized customs procedures.

steps.title: Monthly SPT Filings
steps.description: File VAT by the end of the following month and withholding taxes by the 20th.

steps.title: Annual CIT Return
steps.description: Form 1771 must be filed by April 30th of the following year. Late filing incurs interest penalties.

steps.title: Transfer Pricing (TP) Doc
steps.description: Required if intercompany transactions exceed IDR 10B. Master File and Local File must be ready by year-end.

items.title: NPWP vs Non-NPWP
items.description: Employees without a Tax ID are subject to a 20% surcharge on their tax rate.

items.title: Expatriate Flat Rate
items.description: Non-resident expats are taxed at a flat 20% (PPh 26) unless a tax treaty applies.

items.title: Benefit-in-Kind (BIK)
items.description: Most company-provided benefits (cars, housing) are now taxable income for the employee since 2023.

items.title: Voluntary Disclosure
items.description: Indonesia frequently offers 'Tax Amnesties' or Voluntary Disclosure Programs. Consult a professional before joining one.

items.title: E-Faktur Reliability
items.description: The DJP's online systems (DJP Online) can be slow on filing deadlines (20th and 30th). File 2-3 days early to avoid system timeouts.

items.title: Tax Consultant Licenses
items.description: Ensure your advisor holds a 'B' or 'C' license (BKP) to represent you during audits or at the Tax Court.

heroData.title: Legal & Master Agreements
heroData.subtitle: Bilingual Enforceability
heroData.description: Drafting and vetting Master Service Agreements that comply with Law No. 24 of 2009 while protecting international IP rights.

items.title: Law No. 24 of 2009
items.text: Agreements involving Indonesian entities MUST be in Bahasa Indonesia. English versions can be included, but Bahasa prevails in disputes.

items.title: Prevailing Clause
items.text: Always specify that the Bahasa version is an 'official translation' to satisfy the law while keeping the English version as the primary reference for intent.

items.title: Court Precedents
items.text: Indonesian courts have previously declared English-only contracts void (null and void) even if both parties agreed to English.

steps.title: Tier 1: Amicable Settlement
steps.description: Mandatory 'Musyawarah' (consultation) period of 30-60 days before escalating.

steps.title: Tier 2: Arbitration (BANI)
steps.description: Preferred over public courts. The Indonesian National Board of Arbitration (BANI) is the standard for commercial disputes.

steps.title: Tier 3: SIAC Option
steps.description: For high-stakes contracts, Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) is common, though local enforcement can be complex.

items.title: Waiver of Article 1266
items.description: Necessary to allow contract termination without a court order, a common requirement in Indonesian civil law.

items.title: Intellectual Property
items.description: Explicitly state that IP created during the service belongs to the client, as default labor law can be ambiguous.

items.title: Notary Authenticity
items.description: For certain long-term services, having the agreement notarized (Waarmaking) provides stronger legal standing.

items.title: Bilingual Prevailing Law
items.description: Ensure the contract explicitly states which version (Bahasa vs English) prevails in case of inconsistency, usually the English version for international clients.

items.title: Force Majeure Scope
items.description: In Indonesia, include specific events like 'demonstrations' or 'infrastructure failure' (blackouts) in FM clauses as they are relatively common.

items.title: Termination Notice
items.description: Standard market notice for MSA termination is 30 to 90 days. Always verify if any 'Minimum Term' applies before signing.

faqs.question: Is wet-ink signature required?
faqs.answer: While ITE Law allows digital, many traditional Indonesian counterparties and gov offices still prefer wet-ink with a 'Meterai' (Stamp Duty).

faqs.question: What is the Stamp Duty rate for 2025?
faqs.answer: The single rate is IDR 10,000. Digital stamps (e-Meterai) are now available and mandatory for many government-linked documents.

faqs.question: Can governed law be foreign?
faqs.answer: Yes, but if the service is performed entirely in Indonesia, judges may still apply local mandatory laws (overriding mandatory rules).

heroData.title: Business Software Indonesia
heroData.subtitle: Digital Ecosystems
heroData.description: Deploy the right tech stack for Indonesia, integrating local payment gateways, digital signature platforms, and e-governance tools.

items.title: Midtrans / Xendit
items.description: Leading payment gateways supporting QRIS, Virtual Accounts (VA), and local e-wallets.

items.title: Privy / Vida
items.description: Certified digital signature providers recognized by Indonesian courts and government.

items.title: Jurnal.id / Accurate
items.description: Local ERP and accounting software with built-in Indonesian tax reporting modules.

items.title: QRIS Dominance
items.text: The Quick Response Code Indonesia Standard is now universal. Even B2B vendors are adopting QRIS for real-time reconciliation.

items.title: BI-FAST
items.text: National real-time payment system. Transactions up to IDR 250M cost only IDR 2,500 in fees, making it the standard for B2B transfers.

items.title: E-Wallet Limitations
items.text: Gopay, OVO, and Dana have monthly balance caps (IDR 20M for upgraded accounts) which must be managed for corporate reimbursements.

steps.title: Cloud Localization Check
steps.description: Ensure SaaS providers have servers in-country if handling sensitive government or financial data (PP 71/2019).

steps.title: API Gateway Setup
steps.description: Connect your global ERP (e.g., Salesforce/SAP) to local gateways for automated reconciliation.

steps.title: Privy/NIK Verification
steps.description: Automate identity checks by integrating with the national ID (Dukcapil) database via certified providers.

steps.title: Cybersecurity Audit
steps.description: Validate systems against the newest 2024 BSSN (National Cyber Agency) standards for private sector resilience.

items.title: Hardware Import Taxes
items.description: Laptops and servers imported to Indonesia are subject to high PPh 22 import taxes (up to 10% for non-API holders). Source locally when possible.

items.title: SaaS Withholding (PPh 26)
items.description: Payments to foreign SaaS providers (like AWS or Slack) are technically subject to 20% withholding tax unless a Tax Domicile Certificate (DGT) is provided.

items.title: The 'WhatsApp' Culture
items.description: Almost all local software vendors provide primary support via WhatsApp. Ensure your IT team is comfortable with this informal but rapid communication style.

faqs.question: Is WhatsApp allowed for business logic?
faqs.answer: Yes. WhatsApp Business API is the primary channel for customer support and even internal workflow approvals in Indonesia.

faqs.question: Can I pay employees via E-Wallets?
faqs.answer: Legally, salary must be paid through a banking institution. However, reimbursements and small bonuses are frequently sent via Gopay/OVO.

faqs.question: Do I need a local server?
faqs.answer: For most commercial sectors, cloud servers in Singapore/Australia are acceptable. Only critical infrastructure and public sector data require local Indonesian storage.

heroData.title: Marketing & Advertising
heroData.subtitle: Social & Influencer Growth
heroData.description: Capture the world's most engaged social media audience through TikTok Shop, Shopee Live, and hyper-local influencer campaigns.

items.title: TikTok Shop / Tokopedia
items.text: The merger has created a massive social-commerce platform. Success in 2025 requires 'Live Shopping' capabilities.

items.title: The Power of KOLs
items.text: Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) drive 60%+ of purchase decisions. Localized, niche influencers often outperform high-reach celebrities.

items.title: Halal Labeling
items.text: Mandatory Halal certification for F&B and cosmetics. Marketing materials must respect these cultural sensitivities.

steps.title: Localization of Content
steps.description: Translate and adapt creative assets into 'Gaul' (youth slang) or formal Indonesian depending on the target segment.

steps.title: KOL Vetting & Booking
steps.description: Analyze audience demographics. Ensure they don't have overlapping conflicts with competitors.

steps.title: Media Placement
steps.description: Coordinate with local agencies like Dentsu Indonesia or local boutiques for out-of-home (OOH) billboards in Jakarta's high-traffic zones.

steps.title: Live Stream Ops
steps.description: Set up a physical studio and trained hosts for 24/7 or prime-time Shopee/TikTok live sessions.

items.title: BPOM Restrictions
items.description: Marketing for health/beauty products requires BPOM (Food & Drug) approval on all claims.

items.title: Indonesian Language Law
items.description: While English is common in SCBD, mass-market ads should be predominantly in Bahasa Indonesia.

items.title: Ethical Codes
items.description: Avoid sensitive topics including religion, race, and ethnicity (SARA) to prevent social backlash.

items.title: Performance vs Creative
items.description: Local boutique agencies often excel at creative 'Gaul' content, while international networks provide better performance tracking and attribution.

items.title: Influencer Pricing
items.description: Influencer rates vary wildly. It's common to negotiate packages that include a mix of Feed posts, Stories, and Live appearances.

items.title: Regional Nuances
items.description: What works in Jakarta might not resonate in Medan or Makassar. Consider regional dialects and local icons for provincial campaigns.

faqs.question: Is influencer marketing expensive?
faqs.answer: Micro-influencers can start from IDR 1M per post, while mega-celebs can charge IDR 100M+. Most ROI is found in mid-tier influencers (100k-500k followers).

faqs.question: Can I run ads in English?
faqs.answer: For B2B or ultra-premium products targeting the SCBD crowd, English is effective. For mass-market consumer products, Bahasa is a must.

faqs.question: What is 'Jasa Titip' or Jastip?
faqs.answer: A grassroots personal shopper phenomenon. While not a formal channel, it's a huge informal marketing indicator for global brands entering Indonesia.
